The best AI model… is usually the cheaper one.
Welcome to Agent School — lesson twenty-two.
Everyone wants the biggest, smartest model.
Big models: best at hard reasoning, slower, much more expensive.
Small models: fast, cheap — and great at simple, clear tasks.
Extracting a name from a form?
A small model does it perfectly, for a fraction of the price.
So builders route the work: small model for the easy ninety percent, big model only when the task is truly hard.
How to pick: write ten real examples of your task.
Move up only if it fails.
Upgrade only when the task proves it needs more.
